name: @ohmail/desktop
description: ohmail for macOS, Windows and Linux — a Tauri v2 shell around the ohmail client UI: a standalone client that carries its own mail engine and speaks IMAP to your own server. One directory also builds the served host-client bundle its host mode hands to phones.
//: Ranges, not exact pins, and the same ones the rest of the monorepo uses: an exact pin here puts a SECOND copy of @types/react in the workspace, and two React type identities break apps/webapp's typecheck. In the published mirror npm resolves these fresh; every CI run prints what it got.
//scripts: TWO ARTIFACTS, ONE DIRECTORY. `ui:build:engine` is the WINDOW bundle that belongs in a binary compiled with the Rust `local-engine` feature: the real client and the bridge in src/bridge-fetch.ts. `ui:build:host` is the SERVED bundle host mode hands to a phone (dist-host). Set the vite arm and the Cargo feature together or the halves disagree — a window with a bridge and no commands to call, or commands with nothing to call them. Both go through scripts/build-ui.mjs because a `VAR=1 vite build` prefix is POSIX syntax that cmd.exe reads as a program name, and Windows is one of the three platforms this ships to. THREE halves, not two: the engine-bearing artifact also needs `--config src-tauri/tauri.engine.conf.json`, which is what puts the engine and its Node runtime into the bundle as resources. `app:build:engine` selects all three and is the only thing CI calls. (A third artifact — a fixtures-only interface preview, once `ui:build`'s default — is retired under the no-demo rule; build-ui.mjs refuses a bare invocation so a stale caller learns that rather than getting the window bundle under an old name.)

scripts.//scan: Reads the BUILT bundles for what each may and may not contain — the sample world absent from both (the no-demo rule, with the refusing stub asserted present so the guard cannot go green by deletion), the real sync client present in both, and the gate-only surfaces (local model, hosted suggest, shell commands) in the window bundle alone. Say which artifact you built; the script does not guess, because a leak reaches the bridge and would flip a guess. `app:build:engine` runs both for you.

//devDeps: vitest is here because this project's own tests under test/ are published and import it — a clone should be able to run the suite it can read, not just look at it. MIT.
//deps: The five below are not used by anything under apps/desktop/src — they are imported by the shared client sources this project compiles (the rich text editor in the compose and reply surfaces, the mail renderer's HTML sanitizer, and the PDF renderer behind the attachment Quick Look). They are declared here because this manifest is the only one published with those sources: without them the mirror's `tsc --noEmit` and `vite build` both fail on modules npm was never asked to install. Licences, checked before adding: the TipTap packages and their transitive @tiptap/core and @tiptap/pm are MIT; dompurify is (MPL-2.0 OR Apache-2.0), taken here under Apache-2.0; pdfjs-dist (pdf.js) is Apache-2.0. All are compatible with this repository's AGPL-3.0-only licence.
//engineDeps: The nine below belong to the mail engine — its IMAP client, mail parser, mail sender, on-device database, HTML sanitizer, public-suffix list and archive reader. That engine's source IS in this repository: apps/sidecar over the mail halves of packages/api, core, db, db-mail and services, bundled into one file by scripts/engine-bundle.mjs and packaged beside a checksum-verified Node runtime. Nothing under apps/desktop imports any of them, and neither does anything this project typechecks or bundles — the engine is built from the repository root, resolving these from the manifests published beside its own sources. They stay declared here as the record of what the shipped app carries, and because the licence audit is the part that must not drift. Ranges are the ones the rest of the workspace already resolves. Licences, checked before adding: drizzle-orm and @electric-sql/pglite are Apache-2.0; imapflow, mailparser, tldts, sanitize-html and htmlparser2 are MIT; nodemailer is MIT-0; jszip is (MIT OR GPL-3.0-or-later), taken here under MIT. All are compatible with this repository's AGPL-3.0-only licence.
